comments.text:
One thing that reveals the complete absurdity of the education system is when they try to teach young kids about consent and bodily autonomy.

They're going to have to shush down the loud ones, make the jittery ones sit still in chairs, snap the dreamy ones out of their reverie, and occasionally punish the insufferable one by making them stand alone in a corner (possibly forcibly, but without blows or slaps because that's abuse), while explaining very seriously to all these children that when an adult tells them to do something with their body that they're uncomfortable with, they don't have to obey, they should say no and tell another adult.

It''s as absurd as trying to instill a whistleblower culture in China.

When all of education is geared towards forcing kids to do something they don't want (how many kids in the world are disappointed when school is cancelled?), we shouldn't be surprised when kids indeed do everything adults tell them to do, including never telling anyone.

comments.text: Standardized testing is NOT for the students. It's for the education system. It's metrics. It doesn't measure their knowledge especially for K-12. (Most 18 year olds are not experts in any domain, but they can become experts at something if they go to university.) It measures the progression of their brains' development.  It measures their ability to comprehend, analyze, observe underlying concepts, think critically, and synthesize information CORRECTLY for reading, science, social studies and math. Although standardized testing is imperfect and seems unfair, it tells educators if most students reach the healthy benchmarks for brain and emotional development at every stage of growth or if changes need to be implemented to support students that struggle.
